entries.summary: The completion ping gains a sound: Soft, Chime or Pop, synthesized in the app (no audio files), with a Test sound button in Settings. It only plays when the ping itself fires, and picking a sound previews it.

Settings gains an Accent color picker: Green (the current default), Violet, Blue, Amber, Rose or Teal. It recolors the primary buttons and highlights through one CSS variable, applies instantly, and is kept as part of your settings.

Tools gains Help & shortcuts: one tap prints a help card into the chat covering the answer styles, quick prompts, slash commands and keyboard shortcuts. It is assembled from the app's live tables, so it always matches what the app can actually do.
The status bar now shows the selection size (characters, plus lines when it spans several) and the current file's type (Python, JavaScript, Markdown and friends) next to the cursor position.

Every answer gains a Speak button: the device reads it aloud with markdown flattened (code blocks become a spoken placeholder instead of symbols). Tap again to stop. If the device has no speech engine, the button says so instead of failing silently.

Chat keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+. jumps to the chat box from anywhere, Ctrl+/ toggles Chat options, Ctrl+L clears the chat (with the usual warning), and Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down moves between chats. They stay out of the code editor's way, and a Shortcuts button in Chat options lists them all.

A Find in chat box in Chat options filters the visible messages as you type and counts the matches. It works on everything on screen (your messages, answers, system notes) and clears back to the full chat when emptied.

Every Ghost answer gains two more buttons: Save writes it to a file in the workspace, and Code copies only its code blocks. Your own messages gain Edit & resend: rewind the chat to that message, fix it, and send again (everything after it is removed, with a warning first).

Settings gains a filter box (type to find a setting, sections hide when nothing matches), Export and Import for carrying your settings between devices as JSON (import only accepts known settings with the right types), and a Reset all settings button. Chats and files are never touched.

Choose how much project context rides with each message: a context budget (Lean 3,000 to Huge 20,000 tokens, used by chat, slices, recall and convert alike), a switch for attaching the editor selection, and an opt-in switch that attaches the git diff of your uncommitted changes, capped so it cannot flood the model.

Chat appearance settings: text size (Small, Default, Large), panel width on desktop (Slim to Extra wide), message bubbles, and a toggle for the You / Ghost labels. All apply live and combine with Compact chat.

Type / in the chat box: /explain, /fix, /tests and /doc run the file quick actions (add a note after the command to steer it), /clear clears the chat, /export exports it, /regen repeats the last answer, and /help lists them all.

Export chat as Markdown, plain text, or a standalone web page (fully escaped, safe to share), copy the whole chat at once, and see a running count of messages, words and estimated tokens for the current chat in Chat options.
Editor display settings: line spacing (Tight, Normal, Roomy, Loose), font ligatures on or off, line numbers on or off, and the current-line highlight on or off. All apply live and are remembered.

Creativity (temperature) now lives in Chat options too, with one-tap Precise, Balanced and Creative presets in Settings; both sliders always agree. Answer length gains a Custom choice with your own token count, and after each answer the chat shows how long it took and its estimated speed.

Save the prompt in the chat box under a name, then reuse it in any project from Chat options: pick it, Insert, send. Prompts live on the device, can be replaced by saving the same name again, and can be deleted from the same row.

Every project can now hold several named chats. Switch between them in Chat options, start a new one, rename it, or delete it; each keeps its own history and its own unsent draft. Your existing chat stays as the first one, untouched.

The chat box grows as you type and shows a live character and estimated-token counter. An unsent message is kept as a draft for the project and restored when you come back. Every Ghost answer gains a Copy button, and a Continue button in Chat options picks up a cut-off answer where it left off.

Chat gets an answer style picker (Balanced, Teacher, Code only, Reviewer, Rubber duck), an answer length picker, quick prompt chips, and Regenerate / Copy / Export buttons in the options fold. Settings is grouped into Chat, Editor and Interface, and gains custom instructions for every chat, a history window, a send-key choice, a completion ping toggle, message time stamps, an editor font picker, compact chat and reduce motion.

The Context lab gains an Export section: the current slice is exported by GhostSlice itself into a bundle, then converted by the GhostConvert tool into AGENTS.md, Cursor rules, Copilot instructions, or a generic prompt - with every conversion loss named per format from the tool's own LOSSES.md, and the output verified by the tool before it is shown.
